# Sentinel

[![CI](https://github.com/rxj0102/sentinel/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rxj0102/sentinel/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

A platform for testing behavioral stock signals: six signals with their expected signs locked before any data was seen, a backtest engine, three portfolio constructions, a trial registry that feeds the deflated Sharpe ratio, and a locked holdout. Built on free data only.

It has produced two findings on real data so far, and both are negative.

<!-- headline:start (generated by sentinel readme, do not edit by hand) -->
**1. Free stock-level data cannot carry this test.** The first real rebuild of the point in time S and P 500 found no price history for 39% of index member days in 2005, because the free source drops companies that were acquired, went bankrupt or were delisted. Those are the stocks behavioral signals bet on, so the gate on stock-level results stays shut. [FINDING src=evidence/data_quality/data_quality_coverage_by_year.csv]

**2. On data without that hole, the locked signs do not hold up.** Tested on published portfolios built from the full CRSP universe, 2005-01 to 2022-12: None of the 4 testable signals is confirmed and none is contradicted. 3 of the 4 were statistically significant before 2005, so this is a premium that faded, not one that never existed. [FINDING src=evidence/published/metrics.json]
<!-- headline:end -->

Every number on this page is written by code from the files under evidence/, and CI fails if the page and the files disagree.

## Finding 1: the survivorship hole in free data

The universe is rebuilt from the index change log, and prices come from a free daily source. The table shows how much of the index that source cannot price.

<!-- survivorship:start (generated by sentinel readme, do not edit by hand) -->
| Year | Index member days | Without a price | Members never priced |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2005 | 129780 | 38.6% | 163 |
| 2008 | 130295 | 35.1% | 163 |
| 2011 | 129766 | 32.5% | 155 |
| 2014 | 129820 | 26.1% | 133 |
| 2017 | 130520 | 18.4% | 106 |
| 2020 | 131261 | 11.9% | 67 |

In 2005, 39% of index member days have no price in the free source; by 2022 it is still 9%. The rebuilt member count is 514 to 520 in every one of 216 months, against a target of 500 with a tolerance of 10, so 216 of 216 months fail the reconciliation. [FINDING src=evidence/data_quality/data_quality_coverage_by_year.csv]

What that does to a return: an equal-weight portfolio of the names that do have prices earns 12.8% a year over the window. Charging the missing names a penalty of 5 or 15 percent a year, two assumptions that bracket the problem and are not estimates, lowers it to 11.4% or 8.6%. The spread between those is larger than the premium any signal here is expected to earn. [FINDING src=evidence/data_quality/data_quality_survivorship_sensitivity.csv]
<!-- survivorship:end -->

This is why the repository has a REAL-DATA GATE (docs/REAL_DATA_GATE.md): no stock-level signal result may be cited until the rebuilt universe passes these checks. It was written before the first rebuild, the rebuild failed it, and it stays open. The stock-level engine below is validated on a synthetic market only.

## Finding 2: the locked signs on published portfolios

Amendment 3 of docs/hypotheses.md, committed before these tests were run, moves the real-data evidence to the Open Source Asset Pricing portfolios of Chen and Zimmermann. They are built from the full CRSP universe with delisting returns, so they do not have the hole above. Each locked signal is matched to its nearest published definition, and the mapping, sample, statistic and verdict rules are fixed in the amendment.

<!-- published:start (generated by sentinel readme, do not edit by hand) -->
Value-weighted quintile long-short returns, 2005-01 to 2022-12, 216 months. Positive means the locked sign held. t-statistics use Newey-West errors with 6 lags; p-values are one-sided and Holm-adjusted across the four signals. [FINDING src=evidence/published/metrics.json]

| Locked signal | Published counterpart | Return per year | t | Holm p | Verdict | Before 2005, per year (t) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 52 week high anchoring | High52 | 3.4% | 0.59 | 0.83 | **Not confirmed** | 6.6% (2.43) |
| Lottery stocks (max daily return) | MaxRet | 2.8% | 0.58 | 0.83 | **Not confirmed** | 5.8% (2.27) |
| Realized skewness | ReturnSkew | 2.7% | 1.73 | 0.17 | **Not confirmed** | 0.7% (0.82) |
| Short-term reversal | STreversal | -4.4% | -1.09 | 0.86 | **Not confirmed** | 6.2% (3.10) |
| Equal-weight composite of the four | | 1.1% | 0.45 | 0.33 (unadjusted) | **Not confirmed** | |

How much these tests could see: if each premium were half its pre-2005 size, about what Chen, Lopez-Lira and Zimmermann find survives publication, the chance that the locked test confirms it is 7.7% to 18.8% per signal, before the Holm adjustment makes it harder. So not confirmed here is weak evidence that the premiums are gone: a test this noisy would usually miss a premium of that size. [FINDING src=evidence/published/metrics.json]

The composite has a Sharpe ratio of 0.13 before any trading cost, and the four series have a mean pairwise correlation of 0.08. The last column is context, not a test: those years were public long before the signs were locked. Disposition overhang and abnormal volume have no published counterpart in the release and are not tested. [FINDING src=evidence/published/metrics.json]

Robustness, return per year (t), reported next to the headline and never used to choose it. The first column uses equal weights for three signals and value weights for the lottery signal, whose original paper is value-weighted, so that row repeats the headline:

| Locked signal | Quintiles, each paper's own weighting | Original paper construction |
|---|---|---|
| 52 week high anchoring | 3.8% (0.57) | 2.5% (0.47) |
| Lottery stocks (max daily return) | 2.8% (0.58) | 3.6% (0.64) |
| Realized skewness | 1.9% (0.99) | 1.9% (0.99) |
| Short-term reversal | 3.5% (1.20) | 7.6% (1.84) |
<!-- published:end -->

How to read this:

- The signs were locked from the literature, and the literature was right about the past. Most of these long-short returns were large and significant before 2005. In the 18 years since, none is distinguishable from zero in value-weighted portfolios. That matches the finding of McLean and Pontiff (2016) that anomaly returns shrink after publication. Chen, Lopez-Lira and Zimmermann find that about half of a predictor's return survives the end of its original sample, for published and data-mined predictors alike, and the power line under the table uses that as the benchmark. Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen (2023) read the same literature more favourably; their global factor data is the natural next test, written as an amendment before it is run.
- This track tests the idea behind each signal, not the Sentinel code. The published definitions differ a little from the locked ones, the universe is all of CRSP and not the S and P 500, and no trading cost is charged. A positive result here would not have shown a tradable strategy, and the null does not need costs to hold.
- Two of the six signals cannot be tested this way. The disposition overhang and abnormal volume signals have no published counterpart in the release.
- The holdout from 2023 is still locked. One accidental view of seven holdout returns is disclosed in Amendment 3 and logged in holdout/access_log.csv.

## What is built

Status of the stock-level engine: Phases 1 to 4 (data layer, signals, backtest engine, validation framework, portfolio construction) run on a deterministic synthetic market. Their outputs are engineering checks, not findings.

Where to look first: docs/hypotheses.md (pre-registration and three amendments), docs/REAL_DATA_GATE.md (what blocks stock-level results), ASSUMPTIONS.md (every placeholder default), src/sentinel/published.py (the published portfolios track).

## Python version

Sentinel needs Python 3.11 or 3.12 (the pin is below 3.13). On a Mac, either of these works.

With uv:

    brew install uv
    uv venv --python 3.11 .venv
    source .venv/bin/activate
    uv pip install -e '.[dev,live]'

With pyenv:

    brew install pyenv
    pyenv install 3.11
    pyenv local 3.11
    python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
    pip install -e '.[dev,live]'

## Reproduce
    make all          # lint, types, tests, synthetic quality report, docs gate check

CI runs on a deterministic synthetic market and the frozen files under evidence/, needs no network and no secrets. No stock price from the free source is published; evidence/data_quality holds counts and aggregate statistics only.

    sentinel published run      # rerun the published portfolios tests from the frozen series
    sentinel readme --check     # confirm this page matches evidence/

## Rebuilding real data locally

The rebuild was first run against the live endpoints on 2026-11-15 (index membership and prices worked; the factor files were unreachable that day). The prices stay on your machine and are never published.

    export SENTINEL_USER_AGENT='sentinel-research your-email@example.com'
    sentinel data doctor                         # connectivity check for every host
    sentinel data rebuild --dry-run              # universe only, no price download
    sentinel data rebuild --limit 40             # small smoke test
    sentinel data rebuild                        # full rebuild, log in logs/rebuild.log
    sentinel data quality --fixture data/curated # real data survivorship report

The rebuild stops at the end of the development window, so the holdout is not downloaded.
Optional: set FRED_API_KEY (free key, no card) for macro series.

If the first run fails, see docs/REAL_DATA_RUNBOOK.md for the five most likely failure points and the log line each produces.

## REAL-DATA GATE

No stock-level signal result, figure, or number from Phase 2 onward may appear in any doc until the real-data survivorship report exists and the monthly membership count reconciles to about 500. See docs/REAL_DATA_GATE.md. Outputs from the synthetic fixture are written under results/synthetic [SYNTHETIC-ENGINEERING-ONLY], carry a synthetic label, and CI fails if docs cite them as findings (sentinel docs-check).

## Layout

See docs/PHASE0.md for the architecture, data inventory, hypotheses, and decision log. COSTS.md lists every dependency and its terms. RISK_REGISTER.md tracks risks.

## Deviations from the original brief

Both were approved by the sponsor and are repeated in the methodology paper.

1. Analyst herding is replaced by 52 week high anchoring, because free sources have no point in time analyst forecast history.
2. Option implied skew is forward collection only. Realized skewness is the backtestable substitute.
